method: Effective units per assistant message = (input x1 + cache_write x2 + cache_read x0.1 + output x5) times a model weight (Opus 1.0, Sonnet 0.6, Haiku 0.2; approximate relative costs; unknown families such as 'fable' are weighted 1.0). Messages are deduplicated by message id because one API response is written as several transcript lines. Buckets are 15-minute UTC windows; 'lead' is the main session, every other key is one helper agent. Lead context per turn = input + cache_read + cache_write. A compaction is a compact_boundary record, or a drop of lead context to under half of the previous turn (and more than 50k). Savings, per helper: if the lead had done the work itself, everything the helper read via tools (tool-result size, estimated at 4 characters per token) plus the helper's own output tokens would have sat in the lead's context, minus its short final report which reaches the lead anyway. Every later lead turn re-reads that from cache at 0.1 per token at the Opus weight, until the next compaction clears it. Counterfactual = those tokens x number of lead turns after the helper finished (until the next compaction) x 0.1 x 1.0. Saved = counterfactual minus the helper's actual effective units (negative means the helper cost more than it saved). Lead turns before the oldest surviving transcript line are lost to compaction, so 'observed' counts only turns on disk (a lower bound) and 'with_estimate' adds missing turns at the observed turn rate. A second figure (saved_if_lead_did_work_itself) also charges the lead for one own turn per helper turn at its median context, since doing the work itself means re-reading its whole context on every tool call. Conservative: ignores the one-time cache-write cost of the larger lead context and the lead time spent doing the work itself.

totals.note_lead_before_helpers: LOW CONFIDENCE: transcripts on disk start after the last compaction, so per-turn lead history before then is gone; this figure is the session total from the cost-state record minus helpers minus lead turns on disk, divided by wall-clock hours since session start (idle time included).
